content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day window, especially after sharp spikes in the history.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing recent price momentum.
- After a price spike in history, forecasts often overshoot initially and then correct downward — indicating a failure to account for post-spike mean reversion.
- Model exhibits strong downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (days 20–30), particularly when true prices are stabilizing or recovering.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the middle of the horizon (days 10–20) when true prices are often lower — suggesting overconfidence in short-term continuation.
- Model fails to adjust for mean reversion when prices are trending downward — underestimating the pullback toward prior levels.
- Forecasts are systematically too high when history includes recent high prices, especially if the high is followed by a sharp decline — model overreacts to recent highs.
- Model tends to ignore the influence of the most recent 5–7 days of history when forecasting the next 30 days — leading to persistent underestimation of downward trends.
